audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4 and 5 of the level chart are inverted against their own why-text. win[4] says 'Aurora' while whys[4] reads 'E-W-Q into Explosive Cask is a true all-in — stun her, dump the combo, and Cask her into your tower'. win[5] says 'Gragas' while whys[5] reads 'If Body Slam whiffs she free-pokes with Q, roots you, and blinks the entire all-in'. Level 2 was marked Skill though whys[1] describes you out-valuing her poke outright, and levels 4-5 were marked Gragas though whys[3] opens with 'Genuinely even'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart (Gragas, Gragas, Gragas, Skill, Gragas, Aurora, Gragas) matches the existing prose on every one of those four rows, which is strong evidence the disk chart drifted rather than the text. Win rate is 52.73% over 330 games, so a Gragas-leaning chart is right; it was simply assigned to the wrong stages.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Aurora / Gragas / Gragas / Skill / Gragas / Aurora / Gragas with ratings 3,7,7,5,7,4,7. Level 1 stays Aurora because the early text explicitly describes her chipping you with Q from range and you being weak with one ability.
sources: brief currentText whys[1] whys[3] whys[4] whys[5]

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] and phases[5] carried generic template text that described neither champion's actual spike, and the level-6 row read as a warning when it is your best kill window.
audit.why: Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s and Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s — at 6 you have a displacement that beats her blink if you use it to pin her, which is exactly what spikes[1] already describes. The first-item stage is hers because a whiffed Body Slam (14s) is free Twofold Hex poke, not because Riftmaker is late.
audit.corrected: phases[4] states the Body Slam into drink-auto into cask sequence with the 100s cooldown; phases[5] states the whiff punish.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page names no Aurora ability correctly. It invents 'Twofold Hunt' and uses it everywhere as the tracked cooldown — but the text around it ('her escape', 'burst her off her blink') describes a different ability entirely.
audit.why: Her real kit is Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q, 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, 900 range, recastable to drag the curses back for a second hit), Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s — the blink that also turns her invisible), The Weirding (E, 15/14/13/12/11s) and Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s, leaving a slow zone she can teleport across). The escape the page tells you to track is Across the Veil at 22s, and the poke is Twofold Hex at 9s. Those are two different cooldowns and the page merged them into one fictional name.
audit.corrected: Tracked cooldown is now Across the Veil (22s) with Twofold Hex (9s) named separately as the poke; Between Worlds and its 140s cooldown added to the don'ts.

audit.why: The mirror audit's finding applies from this side too and is worth keeping visible: Drunken Rage's damage reduction runs on a flat 5s cycle so Aurora cannot wait it out, and Barrel Roll's potency rises the longer the cask sits, so standing near a placed cask gets worse over time rather than safer. Both already read correctly on this page.

notes: 'Twofold Hunt' is fabricated — it is a mangling of Twofold Hex (Q), but the page used it to mean her blink, which is Across the Veil (W). I split the two apart rather than just renaming, because tracking a 9s poke and a 22s escape as one cooldown is what made the advice unusable. Remaining 'Twofold Hunt' instances live in lower-value or non-writable spots (loading, ahead, breakdown.mid/spikes/feeding/difficulty, report[1]/[3]/[5]/[9]/[10]/[12]/[13]) and still need a sweep. Level-chart flips proposed as one atomic group across both layers.
